verses.text: Jehoshaphat had great wealth and honor, and he made an alliance with Ahab.
A few years later he went down to visit Ahab in Samaria. Ahab slaughtered plenty of sheep and cattle for Jehoshaphat and the people with him, and persuaded him to go with him to Ramoth Gilead.
King Ahab of Israel asked King Jehoshaphat of Judah, "Will you go with me to Ramoth Gilead?" Jehoshaphat answered, "I'm with you, and my people are with your people. We'll join you in the war."
But Jehoshaphat told the king of Israel, "Please ask the LORD what he has to say first."
The king of Israel gathered four hundred prophets and asked them, "Should we go to war at Ramoth Gilead, or should I hold back?" They said, "Go. God will hand it over to the king."
Jehoshaphat asked, "Is there another prophet of the LORD here we can ask?"

The king of Israel answered, "There's one man we could ask to speak for the LORD, Micaiah son of Imla. I hate him because he always predicts trouble for me and never anything good." Jehoshaphat said, "The king shouldn't talk like that."
So the king of Israel called an officer and said, "Bring Micaiah son of Imla here at once."
The king of Israel and King Jehoshaphat of Judah sat on their thrones in royal robes in the open area at Samaria's gate. All the prophets were prophesying in front of them.
Zedekiah son of Chenaanah had made iron horns. He said, "The LORD says, 'With these you'll drive back the Syrians until they're wiped out.'"
All the prophets said the same thing: "Attack Ramoth Gilead and you'll succeed. The LORD will hand it over to the king."
The messenger sent to get Micaiah told him, "Look, all the prophets are promising good things to the king. Please agree with them and say something favorable."
Micaiah answered, "As surely as the LORD lives, I'll say whatever my God tells me."
When Micaiah arrived, the king asked him, "Micaiah, should we fight at Ramoth Gilead or should I hold back?" He answered, "Go and succeed. They'll be handed over to you."
The king replied, "How many times must I make you swear to tell me only the truth in the LORD's name?"
Micaiah said, "I saw all Israel scattered across the mountains like sheep without a shepherd. The LORD said, 'These people have no master. Let them each go home in peace.'"
The king of Israel told Jehoshaphat, "Didn't I tell you? He always predicts trouble for me and never anything good."
Micaiah said, "Then hear what the LORD says. I saw the LORD seated on his throne with the whole army of heaven standing to his right and left.
The LORD asked, 'Who will lure King Ahab of Israel into going to Ramoth Gilead, where he'll fall?' One suggested one thing and another suggested something else.
Then a spirit stepped forward, stood before the LORD, and said, 'I'll lure him.' The LORD asked, 'How?'
The spirit said, 'I'll go and put lies in the mouths of all his prophets.' The LORD said, 'You'll lure him and succeed. Go and do it.'
So look, the LORD has put a lying spirit in the mouths of these prophets of yours, and the LORD has declared disaster for you."
Then Zedekiah son of Chenaanah came over and slapped Micaiah across the face. He asked, "Which way did the LORD's Spirit go when he left me to speak to you?"
Micaiah answered, "You'll see on the day you go into an inner room to hide."
The king of Israel ordered, "Take Micaiah back to Amon, the city governor, and to Joash, my son.
Tell them the king says, 'Throw this man in prison and give him only a little bread and water until I return safely.'"
Micaiah said, "If you come back safely at all, the LORD hasn't spoken through me." Then he added, "Everyone, listen to this!"
So the king of Israel and King Jehoshaphat of Judah went up to Ramoth Gilead.
The king of Israel told Jehoshaphat, "I'll go into battle in disguise, and you wear your royal robes." So the king of Israel disguised himself, and they went into battle.
The king of Syria had ordered his chariot commanders, "Fight only the king of Israel. Leave everyone else alone, whatever their rank."
When the chariot commanders saw Jehoshaphat, they said, "That's the king of Israel!" They turned to attack him. Jehoshaphat cried out, and the LORD helped him. God drew them away from him.
When the commanders realized he wasn't the king of Israel, they stopped chasing him.
Someone drew his bow at random and hit the king of Israel between the pieces of his armor. The king told his chariot driver, "Turn around and get me out of the battle. I'm badly wounded."
The fighting grew fiercer that day. The king of Israel stayed propped up in his chariot facing the Syrians until evening. Around sunset he died.
